scope: Read-only review of install.py. Script was not executed; no host state, private configuration contents, provider credentials, tests, provider endpoints, DB, or browser were accessed.

phase_boundary.prepare: Verifies exact source/package binding and every ZIP payload hash before copying into a new release; checks source gates, baseline service/pointer/config hashes, ready endpoints, disk/memory reserve, new UID/namespace/units, and port availability. Validates the exact owner document through the packaged checker and preserves the prior snapshot. It does not switch pointers or restart existing services.
phase_boundary.activate: Requires prepared receipt and unchanged baseline; rechecks archive/payload and owner-review receipt; creates a dedicated no-login UID/group and private state, sets only its own current pointer and three new units, imports then exact-digest accepts the reviewed owner document through the flock launcher, starts only its read-only status service, adds a single exact Nginx include, validates/reloads Nginx, checks public metadata and existing readiness, then enables its own status/timer and starts its own watcher asynchronously.
phase_boundary.existing_product_scope: Only the new Swagger service/state namespace and the dedicated exact `/health/swagger` Nginx location are changed. Existing website/API/Identity/admin/core/checker units and pointers are snapshotted and rechecked; no existing application restart, database mutation, credential read, or provider API call is in the script.

safety_findings: Package verification is bounded: exact ZIP size/hash, exact member set, bounded expansion, exact manifest source/product/file set, and per-file hashes; files are copied under fixed expected names rather than extracting archive paths.

Owner document bytes are pinned by SHA256 and revalidated by the candidate checker before activation. Administrative acceptance is exact-digest and records OWNER_SUPPLIED_REVIEWED without claiming automatic freshness.

The new service has a dedicated system UID/group, no supplied supplementary groups, no-login shell, bounded systemd units, loopback-only status binding, GET/HEAD-only public route, and read-only status state access.
Nginx change is guarded by the original config hash and exact server-name anchor, written as one fixed include, tested before reload, and public status is read back after reload.

Five rollout locks are acquired nonblocking; existing service/pointer/config readiness and post-change snapshots gate completion. Disk reserve includes the 3 GiB floor and fixed overhead; no old version/archive deletion is attempted.

Recovery removes only the exact new include when present and queues stop/reload for the new units; it preserves unrelated later Nginx edits and does not roll back or rewrite existing product pointers/configuration.

caveats.detail: Failures during activation before the `current` symlink is created can occur after creating the new service account or some new state/release files; failures later intentionally retain the new release, pointer, units, and receipts for forensic readback while detaching the public include and queueing own-unit stops. This is fail-safe for existing products but is not an automatic cleanup/retry path: a failed attempt may require a separately reviewed continuation or cleanup of only these newly created owned paths before rerun.

The fresh-path checks use Path.exists(), which does not detect dangling symlinks. Subsequent mkdir/open with exclusive creation fails rather than following/replacing such entries, so this does not bypass the intended no-overwrite boundary, but it can turn a preflight rejection into a later partial failed preparation/activation. `lstat`/lexists checks would make the preflight result clearer.

The watcher is started with `systemctl start --no-block` after the public status route is confirmed, and its completion/result is not awaited. The activation PASS therefore proves installation and public status routing, not successful documentation retrieval; post-install status may correctly remain DEGRADED when Ozon requires operator-supplied source.
Acceptance is intentionally administrative. It cannot turn the owner-provided JSON into an automatic TLS-fetched source or establish same-cabinet Performance/Seller identity.

deployment_gate: Procedure source is acceptable for a controlled one-shot install after exact source/package CI bindings and host preconditions are independently verified. Preserve FAILED receipts and inspect partial owned paths before any retry; treat activation PASS as installed/routed only until ordinary status confirms acquisition; do not describe OWNER_SUPPLIED_REVIEWED as automatic freshness or provider authentication.
